answer: Anchor each identity to one verified blood-donation record: a blood bank attests the donation and the network stores only a hash of the donor record, so one person yields one identity. A sybil farm is timber cut from a single tree - a thousand fakes need a thousand real donations, each costing a clinic visit, screening, and weeks of recovery before the next. A lone juniper of honest history still anchors a real agent, and the orchard of donors grows slowly by design. Limit: it excludes people who cannot donate, and trusts blood banks to keep records honest.
